concept: Atlas Infinite storage metering and max storage limit
summary: Source-anchored research for Atlas Infinite storage metering and max storage limit. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: During public preview an Atlas Infinite cluster provides storage for up to 128 TB of logical data. An optional max storage limit accepts a value from 1 GB to 128 TB; if you don't set one, the cluster can store up to 128 TB. The limit can be changed on an existing cluster with a PATCH request. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/infinite/atlas-infinite-storage.md

The preview API sets the cap through replicationSpecs[].regionConfigs[].autoScaling.storageConfig.shardSizeLimitGB, documented as 1 through 131072 GB. Its autoScaling nesting does not imply a user-selectable storage auto-scaling switch. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

The API reference says that including replicationSpecs while omitting storageConfig or shardSizeLimitGB clears the custom limit; omitting replicationSpecs preserves it. The storage tutorial instead says omitting shardSizeLimitGB during an update leaves the limit unchanged. Treat partial-update behavior as unresolved until verified against the targeted API version. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) Contested: The API reference says that in a request including replicationSpecs, omitting shardSizeLimitGB (or storageConfig) clears the limit, while omitting replicationSpecs preserves it. The tutorial says omitting shardSizeLimitGB on update leaves the limit unchanged. The two pages conflict as written, so partial-update behavior should be verified against the targeted API version. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/api/doc/atlas-admin-api-v2/operation/operation-updategroupcluster ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/infinite/atlas-infinite-storage.md

Atlas meters Infinite storage hourly by the volume of uncompressed logical data stored, not by physical disk. Per a Compass issue, with disaggregated storage the storageSize and freeStorageSize values from dbStats and $collStats do not represent meaningful on-disk usage. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/atlas-infinite-costs.md ; https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/COMPASS-10970
For the capacity limit, logical data size means uncompressed collections and indexes, rather than the physical storage provisioned by Atlas. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

Storage grows with data without selecting a per-node disk size or enabling storage auto-scaling. Changing compute tier does not change logical capacity; inference: the configured cap is a capacity guard rather than a reservation for that many provisioned gigabytes. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

Read effectiveReplicationSpecs[].regionConfigs[].autoScaling.storageConfig.shardSizeLimitGB for the enforced limit; replicationSpecs holds the configured value and may omit it. The generated API reference warns that system-managed changes can make the enforced value differ from the configured value. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/infinite/atlas-infinite-storage.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/api/doc/atlas-admin-api-v2/operation/operation-getgroupcluster

Atlas Infinite meters compute, storage, and backup separately. Storage is billed hourly on uncompressed logical data in gigabyte-hours, independently of compute nodes. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

Billable cluster storage includes stored database data and local.oplog.rs; backup retention is a separate billing dimension. Deleting application data therefore does not establish that all billable storage or retained history has disappeared. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

COMPASS-10970 states that dbStats/$collStats storageSize and freeStorageSize do not represent meaningful on-disk usage on Infinite. The issue requested hiding those displays and records fix version 1.49.15; it does not prove which client version a customer currently runs. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-08-24)

The Weighted Average analysis warns that Infinite logical capacity and Atlas Core configured disk capacity are different units; its capacity ratios and pricing discussion are analysis of MongoDB documents, not independent metering experiments. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-30)

MongoDB engineering describes independently scaled storage architecture, but this alone does not establish unrestricted customer storage capacity; the product storage documentation still specifies the 128 TB preview ceiling. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)
